panels.rationale: Single axial brain MRI panel from a case report of confirmed murine typhus (positive typhus serologies, doxycycline-responsive) showing diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement, a recognized but less common CNS manifestation. Disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused article title and the panel-specific captioned manifestation matching the vocabulary term for meningeal enhancement on MRI. Red annotation arrows are present.

in_text_mentions: e and vancomycin were empirically started for meningitis but the patient did not improve. Lumbar puncture was within normal limits. The patient’s condition worsened, and she became hypotensive with the development of DIC. Hypoxic respiratory failure ensued and the patient was intubated. Chest X-ray showed diffuse pulmonary opacities and MRI was positive for leptomeningeal enhancement consistent with meningitis or inflammatory changes (Figure 1). Typhus serologies came back positive and doxycycline was initiated, which led to rapid and complete resolution of symptoms, and the patient recovered.

panels.rationale: Single axial CT pulmonary angiogram panel from a case report titled "Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis-Like Presentation of Murine Typhus in a Previously Healthy Adult"; the caption describes bilateral perihilar ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening (crazy-paving) and the in-text mentions attribute this imaging pattern to the patient's murine typhus. Real patient imaging, red arrows annotate the abnormalities. Ground-glass opacities/septal thickening are not in the provided vocabulary, so they are recorded as proposed findings; the closest vocabulary entry (interstitial infiltrates) is tagged with the caption evidence. Atypical because the article frames this as a rare alveolar-proteinosis-like pulmonary presentation.
panels.attribution_text: Pan and Sweet. Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis-Like Presentation of Murine Typhus in a Previously Healthy Adult.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.114577. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: CT chest pulmonary angiogram Bilateral perihilar ground-glass opacities and interlobular septal thickening are observed (red arrows).
in_text_mentions: Due to concern for community-acquired pneumonia, the patient was started on ceftriaxone and azithromycin, and IV fluids. CT pulmonary angiogram was negative, but CT imaging (Figure 1) revealed bilateral perihilar ground‑glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening, a pattern characteristic of "crazy‑paving.” Chest radiograph showed left perihilar opacity and pleural effusion. Empiric antibiotics remained ineffective in alleviating symptoms.

plate_findings.evidence: (A) Chest x‐ray on PICU admission showed diffuse bilateral air‐space opacities with bronchogram and right pleural effusion.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Disease-focused case-report title (atypical presentation of murine typhus with ARDS) plus in-text link between this admission chest radiograph and the patient's murine typhus illness; the panel shows captioned alveolar/air-space opacities matching the pulmonary manifestation supported by the vocabulary. The presentation is explicitly atypical. B: Thoracic CT from the same murine typhus case report (atypical ARDS/septic shock presentation) showing captioned bilateral diffuse alveolar opacities suggestive of alveolar hemorrhage and ground-glass areas. No vocabulary key covers ground-glass/alveolar hemorrhage on CT, so findings are proposed; hepatosplenomegaly mentioned in the text is not visible on this thoracic panel. The reported pulmonary involvement is the atypical presentation of the disease.
panels.attribution_text: François et al. A 16-Year-Old Boy With ARDS and Septic Shock, an Atypical Presentation of Murine Typhus: Case Report and Review of the Literature.. Case reports in critical care 2026. doi:10.1155/crcc/1267884. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Chest x‐ray on PICU admission showed diffuse bilateral air‐space opacities with bronchogram and right pleural effusion. (B) Thoracic CT scan showed bilateral and symmetrical diffuse alveolar opacities suggestive of alveolar hemorrhage and areas of ground glass suggestive of underlying infection and pleural effusions.
in_text_mentions: ry failure with hemoptysis. Because of lack of improvement on noninvasive ventilation, he was intubated a few hours after his arrival. He quickly developed severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Chest x‐ray showed an alveolar infiltrate (Figure 1A). A thoracoabdominal CT scan (Figure 1B) showed bilateral and symmetrical diffuse alveolar opacities suggestive of alveolar hemorrhage and areas of ground glass suggestive of an underlying infection, as well as pleural effusions, hepatomegaly, and perivesicular oedema. Protective ventilation was introduced with prone positioning sessions.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Day-1 axial chest CT of a patient with murine typhus showing bilateral lower-lobe patchy infiltrates (black arrow) with small pleural effusion; pulmonary involvement is a recognized manifestation of murine typhus, though radiographic findings are less classic than the rash. B: Companion day-1 axial chest CT slice showing bilateral lower-lobe infiltrative opacities (black arrow) in the murine typhus patient; same pulmonary involvement as panel A. C: Day-6 chest CT showing progression of bilateral infiltrates with increased pleural effusion during murine typhus with severe systemic involvement; support tubes visible but the lung pathology remains the target finding. D: Sixth-day axial CT slice confirming worsening bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and pleural effusion in the same murine typhus patient (ICU, mechanically ventilated).

Blood, urine, and stool cultures were obtained, and empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone, and metronidazole were initiated for presumed sepsis of gastrointestinal origin
